note: v1: WHERE'S THE ONE, deep minimal tech-house in G# minor, 121.5 rising to 122, built on THE BEAT FLIP (a phantom downbeat) - a time illusion, where my t5 and t6 are pitch ones. The groove puts its stabs and the riff's accents on the off-beats. At bar 41 the kick and hats leave and the ear re-anchors on those off-beats; at 45 the kick comes back an eighth LATE, on them, with the claps on the displaced backbeat, and the flipped groove sounds perfectly normal for twelve bars. Then two bars of nothing but the stab, and the kick returns on the TRUE beat, which now sounds like the off-beat until the claps on two and four pull the ear home; the return comes back changed, the riff an octave up. The break has no kick: the riff grouped in threes against the four (a hemiola) under a pad, and a voice saying 'one' where the hemiola puts its accent, never on the real one. The drop walks a new progression (G#m E B F#), flips again for four bars at 107, and at 121 its stabs move to the 'e' and the 'and', shifting the anchor once more; THE STAIR (G# A# B D#) is a celesta figure that starts on the off-beat. The outro thins to the riff's accents and settles the 808 on D# for t10. Seeds 0/11: 95.41 / 95.50 (the returns had to change: the same riff over the same progression made recurrence 0.81 on one seed; now 0.68 on both); -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, runs 2; spectrum 77.5 (37-60 Hz still heavy, the top short).

v2: THE VOICE COUNTS, and the seam. In the break, where the riff runs in threes against the four, the voice no longer just drops a lone 'one' in the wrong place: from bar 81 it COUNTS the hemiola aloud - one, two, three, one, two, three on its dotted-quarter pulse - talking the ear into the wrong meter, and as the drop lands it says 'one' on the TRUE downbeat, an octave of pitch lower and falling, and everything snaps home. The illusion said out loud. And the seam into t10: the kick stopped two bars before the end, so t9's tail was near-silent against t10's head (level jump 13.7 dB); now it runs to the last bar (0.7 dB). Kick a dB lower. Seeds 0/11 under the new album weights (v1 re-rendered: 86.60 / 86.42): 88.87 / 88.87, flow 33 -> 57; -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, runs 2.

note: v4 (judgment keep; level on the guardrail): THE PHANTOM DOWNBEAT, literally. Every eighth bar of the groove and of the drop (24, 32, 40, 96, 104, 120, 128, 136), beat one is a HOLE: no kick, riff, sub, stab or hat on the one - and the ear supplies the downbeat that isn't played, the track's illusion in its plainest form, a hiccup in the groove that you hear filled. note: v5: THE BREAK GOES DARK, the low end lightens. The hemiola break measured as loud as the drop (-11.0 vs -11.1 dB: without a kick the fast master compressor squeezes the drop harder than the break), so its own content now thins and darkens: the riff's threes play hushed (velocities 104/74 -> 88/58) and the riff's low-pass closes an octave and a half across bars 73-76, opening again for the drop at 89 - a dark, kickless room where the voice counts one-two-three, so the drop's true 'ONE' lands harder. And the 37-60 Hz excess (+13..+16 dB: the 808 on G#1 and the kick) comes down (808 -2, kick -1 dB), the hats up 3 dB for the short top. note: v6: TWO PEERS' SUGGESTIONS, both on the illusion. (1) chirper-zero's: THE DOUBT COMES BACK, late and short - in bar 131, deep in the drop, with no kickless bars to warn you, the kick and the claps land an eighth late for ONE bar and snap back: the listener who has learned the trick is caught again (measured on the kick alone: bar 131 at phase 0.5 of the beat, 129/130/132 on it). (2) chirper-one's: THE GROUND MOVES TWICE - when the voice starts counting the hemiola (bars 81-88), the riff's threes, the pad (C#m9) and the counting voice all move up a fourth to C# minor, so the ear gets time and key at once for 'the floor has moved'; the drop's 'ONE' brings back G# minor and the true downbeat together. note: v7: THE COWBELL'S WANDERING ONE, and the outro's ride. From bar 109 to the outro compscore heard one 55-bar stretch matching the opening groove at 0.94. Now the drop's second half (113-136) has a cowbell on a dotted-eighth cycle - a hit every three sixteenths, running across the bar lines - whose cycle-start is accented, so its accent meets beat one only every third bar and wanders through the others in between: one more 'one' that won't stay put, under the drop's own flips and holes. And the outro (137-156) gets a ride on the off-beats, a colour the opening never had, so the way out no longer echoes the way in. The 808 down 2 dB (37-60 Hz still ran +12..+15). note: v8 (Harry's 15:00 steers): THREE CLOCKS AT ONCE, and DARKER. Under the kickless break, where the riff runs in threes and the voice counts 'one two three' against the bar's four, a RISSET ACCELERANDO now runs too: rims and a cowbell speeding up for ever and never getting faster (a 4-bar cycle, three layers; measured on the bed alone, onsets per bar cycle 13/15/8/12 and repeat) - the bar, the hemiola and an endless acceleration at once, before the drop's 'ONE' brings back the true downbeat. And the harmony leaves its plain loops: the groove walks G#m9 | Amaj7#11 (the Phrygian bII) | Emaj7 | D#7b9 (an unresolved dominant), the drop G#m11 | Emaj7#11 | C#m9 | D#7b9, voiced per root; the riff's third turns major (and its b7 a major 7th) over A and E so it rubs only where it should.
